Package sc.fiji.snt.tracing.auto

Class RootDetector

java.lang.Object
sc.fiji.snt.tracing.auto.RootDetector
public class RootDetector extends Object
Detects candidate locations where several unconnected primary paths - e.g. tracings whose own soma wasn't imaged, or simply not yet joined to one - may converge on a shared, unimaged origin, and reports them as ranked SeedPoints.

Mirrors TuftDetector, but at the opposite topological end: instead of clustering a tree's own terminal structure (tips converging on a tuft), it clusters the root node of every unconnected, non-soma primary Path pooled across the scanned Trees.

Unlike tuft candidates - which already belong to the same tree, so proximity only corroborates something already topologically true - root candidates come from independent fragments with no prior relationship: proximity is the only evidence tying them together. So, unlike TuftDetector, a root with no other root nearby is not reported: on its own it's most likely just an ordinary, complete reconstruction, not a genuine unimaged-soma candidate.

Author:
Tiago Ferreira

      public List<SeedPoint> detect(Collection<Tree> trees)
      Detects root-convergence candidates pooled across every Tree in trees - deliberately not per-tree, since the whole point is catching fragments that live in structurally unrelated Trees (or unconnected primary paths within one).
      Parameters:
      trees - the trees to scan
